questions.q: How does ABAC make an access decision, as distinct from RBAC?
options: It grants access to every authenticated user by default
It requires abandoning roles entirely before it can be used
It evaluates a policy against attributes at the moment of the request, rather than checking a fixed role assigned in advance
It only works for file systems, never for databases or applications
questions.explain: ABAC evaluates attributes fresh on each request against a policy, instead of relying on a static role assignment.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an environment attribute in an ABAC policy?
options: The specific action being attempted, such as read or delete
Whether the requester's device is reporting as compliant with device management policy
The user's job title
A document's sensitivity label
questions.explain: Device compliance, time of day, and network location are environment attributes — contextual conditions at request time.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real tradeoff of using ABAC instead of RBAC?
options: ABAC is more flexible and granular, but harder to design and audit because access depends on evaluating conditions, not reading a membership list
ABAC is always less secure than RBAC in every scenario
There is no real difference in audit complexity between the two models
ABAC requires no policy design at all, unlike RBAC
questions.explain: A role assignment is simple to audit by listing members; an ABAC policy requires reasoning through conditional logic.

questions.q: In the hospital scenario from this lesson, why can't RBAC easily express "a doctor may read only their currently assigned patients' records, during an active shift"?
options: RBAC can express this exact condition natively without any extra roles
RBAC cannot grant any access to patient records under any circumstances
Doing so under RBAC would require a separate role per doctor per shift, which amounts to role explosion
Hospitals are not permitted to use RBAC for legal reasons
questions.explain: RBAC's static roles have no native way to narrow access to this specific, changing condition without creating excessive roles.

questions.q: What does an ABAC policy combine to reach an access decision?
options: User, resource, environment, and action attributes, combined with Boolean logic
Only the user's department, with no other inputs
The user's password strength and login history exclusively
A single fixed permission list with no conditions
questions.explain: A real ABAC policy draws on multiple attribute categories combined with conditional logic, such as "Finance users may read Confidential-Finance records during business hours from a compliant device."
